description:
The dispatch script refuses whenever main's tracker has uncommitted changes, so leads bypass it in three different ways. This lets dispatch proceed over uncommitted data-root changes while every other uncommitted tracked change still blocks.

## Background

`.agents/skills/jit-execution-lead/scripts/dispatch-worker-worktree.sh` exits 1 when `git diff --quiet` or `git diff --cached --quiet` fails on main. On a shared checkout the data root (`.jit/` in this repository) is almost always dirty, because sessions append tracker events and leave them uncommitted until their next tracker commit. A worktree branches from main's commit and never reads main's uncommitted tracker state, so that dirt cannot reach a worker. Leads currently work around the guard three ways: a private copy that excludes `.jit/` by path, a tracker commit made only to pass the guard, and the same private copy in earlier sessions. The script's pre-dispatch snapshot already records every dirty path, so the leak check keeps its baseline. `references/worktree-dispatch-protocol.md` Step 1 states that main must be clean. jit resolves the data root from `JIT_DATA_DIR` or by discovery (`crates/jit/src/main.rs`), and no jit command reports the resolved path today: `jit worktree info --json` names the checkout root but not the data root. Scope extended by the steward's ruling (option a, 2026-11-04): this task exposes the resolved data root once through `jit worktree info`, so tools stop re-deriving jit's discovery rules.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `dispatch-worker-worktree.sh` dispatches when the only uncommitted changes, staged or unstaged, are under the repository's data root, which it obtains from `jit worktree info` rather than embedding a path, and still exits 1 naming the paths when any other tracked file has an uncommitted change.
- [hard] REQ-02: `jit worktree info` reports the absolute resolved data root as one read-only field in its JSON output, with a matching human output line, and the `--schema` contract for the command includes the field.
- [hard] REQ-03: `test-worktree-cache.sh`, the script's existing self-test, covers both cases: a dirty data root dispatches, and a dirty tracked file outside it refuses.
- [hard] REQ-04: The script's header, its success message and `references/worktree-dispatch-protocol.md` describe the guard as it now behaves.

## Notes

Requested by the steward session under `@/inv/convention-convergence`: the guard changes at its source. Once this lands, leads delete private copies of the script.
title: Dispatch over an uncommitted tracker on main
